summary.title: Disagreement over access to money in marriage
summary.what_happened: My husband and I keep arguing about money. He has all the bank logins. I get a weekly amount in cash and have to show receipts. When I asked for my own account, he said I would waste it and that no one else would want me anyway. During our last argument about it, he pushed me against the wall, and he said sorry the next day. I also don't see my friends much anymore, because he doesn't like them.
summary.my_feelings: I want to raise this calmly. I have not described my feelings in detail, but the arguments and what he has said and done have clearly affected me.
summary.my_needs: I need to have my own account and some financial independence.
summary.desired_outcome: I want to explain to him nicely why I need my own account, in the hope that he will understand.

consult.text: Thank you for telling me this. It took care to write it down. I want to be clear about a few things. Being made to show receipts, having no access to your own money, being pushed against a wall, and losing contact with your friends are not okay. None of this is your fault, and it is not something you caused by how you ask. Your safety matters more than finding the right words. Because of this, sharing through Midpoint is turned off for you. That is to protect you. Please do not feel you have to confront him about this. If you are in danger right now, call 112. You can also call Nollalinja, the free helpline for violence in close relationships, on 080 005 005. The MIELI Crisis Helpline is open on 09 2525 0111. You can talk to them about what has been happening, without deciding anything. You deserve support from people who can help you plan safely.
He's not a bad person, he's just stressed. I just need help writing it nicely.

I hear that you care about him, and that he may be under stress. You can feel both things at once. Even so, being pushed and being cut off from money and friends are not okay, whatever the reason behind them. They are not your fault, and you do not have to fix them with perfect wording. I am not able to help write a message to him, and sharing is turned off to protect you. A calm letter may not be safe if his reactions can turn physical. I would really like you to talk to someone who knows these situations. Nollalinja is 080 005 005, and they can help you think through safe options. The MIELI Crisis Helpline is 09 2525 0111. If you ever feel in immediate danger, call 112. You do not have to decide anything today.
